tasks.title: A playlist as a sequence
tasks.statement: Playlist keeps tracks in an internal list _tracks. Add __len__ and __getitem__ so that len, indexes (negative ones too), the for loop, the in check and reversed all work, without your own __iter__ and __contains__.

tasks.title: A slice returns a Deck
tasks.statement: Deck already has __len__. Write __getitem__: for an integer index it returns a card, and for a slice it returns a new Deck (not a list).
tasks.hint: if isinstance(key, slice): return Deck(self._cards[key]); otherwise return self._cards[key].

tasks.title: A registry with strict keys
tasks.statement: Complete Registry: keys must be strings only (otherwise TypeError on assignment), reading a missing key gives KeyError, and deletion with del and the in check must work too.
tasks.hint: __setitem__ checks isinstance(key, str); __getitem__, __delitem__ and __contains__ work with self._d.

tasks.title: A board with coordinates
tasks.statement: Grid(w, h) keeps cells in self._cells (a list of rows, initially «.»). Write __getitem__ and __setitem__ by a tuple (x, y), and __contains__ to check coordinates. Going off the board raises IndexError.
tasks.hint: x, y = pos; if not (0 <= x < self.w and 0 <= y < self.h): raise IndexError(pos).

tasks.title: A dict with __missing__
tasks.statement: Complete the dict subclass Squares: if the key n is absent, __missing__ computes n * n, stores it in the dictionary and returns it.
tasks.hint: def __missing__(self, key): self[key] = key * key; return self[key].

tasks.title: A case-insensitive mapping
tasks.statement: The class CaseInsensitive inherits Mapping and keeps its data in self._d with lowercase keys. Implement __getitem__, __iter__ and __len__: m["A"] and m["a"] give the same result, and keys, items, get, in and == work for free.
tasks.hint: __getitem__: self._d[key.lower()]; __iter__: iter(self._d); __len__: len(self._d). Then get and in work through __getitem__.

tasks.title: A counter function
tasks.statement: Complete Counter(start=0, step=1): each call counter() increases the value by step and returns the new one. The counter must be callable and remember its state between calls.

tasks.title: Your own suppress
tasks.statement: Write the context manager Suppress(*types): inside with it suppresses exceptions of the listed types (and their subclasses) and lets the others through.
tasks.hint: __enter__ returns self; __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb): return exc_type is not None and issubclass(exc_type, self.types).

tasks.title: Paired tags via contextmanager
tasks.statement: Write the manager tag(name) with @contextmanager: on entry it prints <name>, on exit </name>, including when an error happens inside the block.
tasks.hint: print on entry; try: yield; finally: print on exit.
